To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phototransformation of n-alkane-thiol-derivatizated noble metal nanoparticles is dependent on metal, alkanthiol, and solvent, and the transformation is mainly due to the thermalized photon energy.

the phototransformation of alkanethiol-protected noble metal nanoparticles is governed by the interplay between the photon-initiated fragmentation, the thermal-induced melting and vaporization, and the chemical-induced dissociation of alkanethiols.

the fragmentation of n-alkyl-thiol-derivatzed silver nanoparticles is initiated by the photon energy and that the fragmentation efficiency is affected by the solvent polarity and chain length of alkanethiol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photothermal effect of noble metal nanoparticles.
the photothermal transformation of alkanethiol- derivatized metal nanoparticles.
the phototransformation of n-alkylthiol-derivatied noble metal nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
photon energy is converted to heat and then to chemical potential of the metal atoms, and this chemical potential is used to dissociate the alkanethiol and then to fragment the particles.
photon-initiated shape transformation is a result of the interplay between the photon absorption, thermal dissipation, and the reactivity of the particle surface.

the photon-induced shape transformation of n -alkanethiol derivatized nanoparticles is a combination of the following three effects: 1) thermalization, 2) melt, and 3) vaporization, and the relative importance of the three effects depends on the nature of metal, solvent, and alkanethiol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shape transformation is initiated by a photon-induced dissociation of alkanethiol and followed by the fragmentation of the dethiolated nanoparticles.
the shape transformation of alkanethiol-protected noble metal nanoparticles is a complex process, which is influenced by the metal, alkanthiol, solvent, and photon energy.

shape transformation of metal nanoparticles upon photon irradiation is a combination of the following processes, in order of occurrence: 1) thermal conduction, 2) melt and vaporization, 3) dethiolation, 4) fragmentation, 5) recombination, and 6) reformation.

the transformation of metal nanoparticles can be controlled by varying the nature of metal, alchanthiol, and solvent.
the shape transformation of alkanethiol-protected noble metal nanoparticles can be tuned by the choice of metal, aliphatic chain, and solvent.
the shape transformation is a complex process involving multiple factors.
